gaps: A project objective links increasing water deficit with intended prevention of water-use conflict near Nicoya. It does not establish an observed conflict mechanism or evaluated peace outcome; no full pathway is forced.
Indigenous land violence is documented elsewhere, but no inspected passage connects it to climate hazards or adaptation interruption. These issues are not causally joined.
The NAP report's coverage figures are internally ambiguous: 179 products reportedly covered differs from 232 minus 56 unknown. Status tallies are implementation reporting, not resilience impacts.
The regional proposal relies on older records and secondary government analyses; a Brunca risk projection without a source-stated period was excluded.
The undated project registry gives aims and durations, not verified current delivery or completed outcomes. Geographic references to Talamanca and Valle de la Estrella are not conflated.

executive_assessment.text: Named provinces and regions face different agricultural, road, water and coastal livelihood pressures. Acosta offers one dated storm-isolation and community-recovery case.
The 2026 NAP progress review identifies implementation and finance gaps, but its product-coverage figures require reconciliation and do not establish adaptation outcomes.
Water-user conflict prevention near Nicoya, Indigenous family farming, Huetar Norte farms and Paquera-Tambor fisheries are project designs in an undated registry, not delivered or evaluated effects.
